subject: Post-demo: ramp plan, target $/1M ranges, and model-mix options
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@parcelsync.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: ramp plan, target $/1M ranges, and model-mix options

Thanks for your time today — great demo and really helpful to see the real routing patterns. Quick written recap and three pricing scenarios so we can align on next steps: you asked for visibility on unit economics at scale and how adding a separate embedding route changes blended pricing. I attached a short spreadsheet with modeled scenarios.

Key asks (from our side):
- Confirm expected token volumes by month for months 0, 3, and 12 (you mentioned a mid-term ramp).
- Confirm which model(s)/routes you plan to run in parallel (generation vs. embeddings / retrieval).
- Confirm target $/1M tokens you see as acceptable for the steady-state phase (you mentioned wanting sub-$900 if possible).

What I attached: parcelsync-pricing-scenarios-20270915.xlsx — three scenarios in the sheet (Conservative, Baseline commit, Aggressive commit + route mix). High level numbers here so we can move to a draft commercial.

Top-line scenarios (short):
1) On-demand (no commit) — expected $/1M: $1,250 — for teams that need full flexibility.
2) Short commit (3 months) — expected $/1M: $640 — partial commit, smaller discount.
3) 12-month commitment + add embedding route (blended) — expected blended $/1M: $320 — assumes 60% of tokens are cheaper embedding traffic.

Notes on blended math: when you add an embeddings-only route we treat it as a separate SKU with different unit pricing; the spreadsheet shows how a 2-route mix yields the blended figure above at the volumes you sketched.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the 3-month ramp numbers and whether you want embeddings on a separate route.
- If you can share a draft PO or target monthly budget range, I can run a committed-tier pricing exercise and send back a short commercial one-pager.
- Availability: I can join a decision call Tue 9/21 between 10–12 PT if that works — happy to bring Marissa to discuss deal structure.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: parcelsync-pricing-scenarios-20270915.xlsx

From: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@parcelsync.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Kim <a.kim@parcelsync.ai>
Date: 2027-09-16T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ramp plan, target $/1M ranges, and model-mix options

Alex — thanks, this is helpful and the spreadsheet gives a clear view. A few clarifications from our side:

- Current baseline: ~30M tokens/month today (mostly generation).
- Planned ramp: 150M tokens/month by month 3 (we expect the new feature to drive usage), and a potential 400M tokens/month peak by month 12 if the pilot converts.
- Embeddings: we plan to add embeddings for similarity search (expected to be smaller per-request tokens but higher QPS); approximate split by month 3: 70% generation / 30% embeddings.
- Budget: our initial budget for Q4 is modest — $3k–$5k/month — but we have flexibility if the unit economics under a committed plan get us toward the target of <$900 /1M tokens steady state.

Questions for you:
1) For the blended $320 /1M you show in scenario 3, what assumptions on token mix and model SKUs are you using?
2) If we commit to a 6-month ramp (instead of 12), how does that change the blended rate?
3) Are there minimum monthly commit levels for the 12-month tier?

We'd like a short one-page proposal we can take to procurement — show committed levels, illustrative monthly invoices, and the legal contact to expedite a PO. If you can get Marissa to sign off on a draft, we'll loop procurement and legal.

Thanks — happy to hop on Tue 9/21, 10:30 PT if that works.

—Jamie
VP, Product | ParcelSync
jamie.ortiz@parcelsync.ai

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@parcelsync.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-16T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ramp plan, target $/1M ranges, and model-mix options

Jamie — great questions, answers inline below and I updated the attached commercial grid (redwood-pricing-grid-v3.xlsx) with a 6-month ramp variant.

1) Blended $320 /1M assumptions:
   - Model mix at steady state: 60% embeddings (cheaper per-token SKU), 40% generation (higher-cost SKU).
   - Embedding SKU assumed at $95 /1M tokens, generation SKU at $700 /1M tokens in the aggressive commitment model.
   - Blended = 0.6 * 95 + 0.4 * 700 = $320 (rounded).

2) 6-month ramp impact:
   - The 6-month ramp reduces overall commitment term but still allows an intermediate discount. Blended example (6-month commit): $/1M ~ $420 given the same mix and an elevated short-term price for generation tokens; spreadsheet tab "6m-ramp" shows sensitivity at 30/70 and 70/30 splits.

3) Minimum monthly commit for 12-month tier: Yes — we typically require a minimum monthly commitment equivalent to 100M tokens/month for the deepest discounts; we can tier commitments if you need a custom structure (e.g., start at 50M/month for Q1 with a planned uplift schedule).

Proposal I will send after internal sign-off includes: monthly invoice samples, phrased commitment levels, and a draft SOW + legal contact. If you confirm the Month 0 / Month 3 / Month 12 target numbers, I will move this to a commercial draft and include a 90-day promotional discount option to help get the pilot started (proposed 15% off billed consumption for first 90 days).

Next steps:
- Can you confirm Month 0 / Month 3 / Month 12 targets? (30M / 150M / 400M as you suggested is fine for modeling if that is accurate.)
- Confirm whether embeddings should be on a separate route (recommended) so we can show the explicit blended math.
- I'll propose Tue 9/21 10:30 PT and send an invite if that works.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-pricing-grid-v3.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-17T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo: ramp plan, target $/1M ranges, and model-mix options

Alex — quick internal: procurement-approved discretionary discount up to 10% for standard commits; the requested 15% promo needs CRO OK but I can make the case for a pilot concession given strategic fit. Ben — can you run the unit-econ at 10% and 15% variant for the 6m and 12m commits? Include expected ARR uplift and payback timeline in the note.

If it looks good, I'll prep the commercial one-pager and loop Legal (we should use our standard committed-tier terms and append a short pilot addendum).

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
